rilua 0.1.27, vendored for atlantis4-script (Atlantis Evolution's Lua 5.1
scripts).

Origin: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rilua/0.1.27/download
SHA-256 of the .crate: 275971987852cab64d21d060e310b52982a7d9ffbac51acd654a1fd47ebad28b
Upstream: https://github.com/wowemulation-dev/rilua
Licence: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE), unchanged.

Kept from the package: Cargo.toml (as published), Cargo.toml.orig,
Cargo.lock, the licences, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, src/, tests/,
examples/, benches/. Left out: repository tooling (.github, .cargo,
.config, docs, scripts, rust-toolchain.toml and dot files).

The crate is excluded from the Native workspace (its dev-dependencies stay
out of Native's lock file). Its own test suite runs from this directory:
  cargo test --manifest-path vendor/rilua/Cargo.toml

Changes made in Native, each in its own commit with a reproducer test in
crates/atlantis4-script/tests/table_order.rs, so that tables iterate in
PUC-Rio Lua 5.1.4's order: see PATCHES below.

PATCHES

1. src/vm/table.rs, src/vm/execute.rs: `SETLIST` growing the array part
   rebuilds the hash part as PUC-Rio's `luaH_resizearray` does (it calls
   `resize`, which reinserts the hash nodes from last to first). rilua
   only extended the array, so constructors whose last item is a call
   (most nested layouts) iterated in another order.

2. src/vm/table.rs (`new_key`): a main position whose value is nil is
   taken by the new key, as in PUC-Rio's `newkey`. rilua reused it only
   once the old key's string had been collected, so a global set to nil
   and a later new global (ChangeWarp's callback resets) ended in another
   order.

3. src/vm/state.rs, src/stdlib/mod.rs, src/stdlib/package.rs: the
   globals table is created with `luaH_new(L, 0, 2)` and the libraries are
   opened in Lua 5.1.4's `linit.c` order, each registering its globals in
   PUC-Rio's order (`_G`, `base_funcs`, `_VERSION`, `ipairs`, `pairs`,
   `newproxy`; `package`, `module`, `require`); `package.loaded` receives
   the libraries opened after `package` at the end. A fresh `pairs(_G)`
   then walks in Lua 5.1.4's order.
